justification: Changes what served surfaces claim about our own methods, and changes a served confidence value. The paid shadow PDF and the public /how-it-works page stop naming pvlib (zero import sites anywhere in the repo) as our solar-position method. Granny-flat reports stop treating detector-vs-detector count equality as corroboration: 'high' now requires a human-reviewed count, which moves 8 of 16 historical-shape reports from high to medium and adds the amber confidence finding to their PDF. New keys are written into granny_flat_reports.inputs and the confirm write stops deleting the detect row's detected_structures. Served claim + served value + production write shape = critical.

falsifiable_check.command: git grep -nE "^\\s*(import|from)\\s+pvlib" -- . ; git grep -n pvlib -- frontend-nextjs/lib/pdf frontend-nextjs/app/how-it-works services/shadow_detector.py ; git grep -n "PC_CATALOG|S1_COLLECTION" -- services/ ; python -m pytest tests/test_granny_flat_logic.py tests/test_granny_flat_mutation.py -q ; cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest --testPathPattern="granny-flat-confirm-wiring|GrannyFlatBriefCard"
falsifiable_check.passes_when: pvlib has no import site anywhere (grep 1 empty); no served shadow surface and no audit-trail source string names pvlib (grep 2 empty); the deleted SAR endpoint constants have no remaining definition (grep 3 empty); granny-flat confidence reaches 'high' only when confirmed_count_source is 'secondary_detections_classified'; ConfirmationPanel invokes onCountChange with the answer-adjusted count and lifts the per-structure answers to its caller.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Grep 1 returning a hit would mean pvlib IS imported and the reworded copy is itself the false claim. Grep 2 returning a hit means a served surface still names a library the code never runs. Grep 3 returning a hit means a SAR constant survived the deletion. test_high_needs_human_reviewed_count goes red the moment the count_source condition is dropped and detector self-agreement can buy 'high' again. The ConfirmationPanel wiring tests go red if onCountChange stops being called, which is the original defect returning. Each of these compares the code against something outside itself - the import graph, the rendered strings, the caller's observed behaviour - never against its own recomputed output.
falsifiable_check.demonstrated_failing: Every claim was measured against origin/main 0c41c09d and production before any edit, and two pre-change states were reproduced red. (1) Applying the new count_source condition to the existing test suite turned 10 tests red on first run - test_high_requires_all_three, test_zero_counts_agree_high, test_confidence_high_when_all_good and 7 others were all asserting that count equality alone earns 'high'. Those failures ARE the old doctrine being exercised; each was flipped with an in-test reason rather than deleted. (2) Production measurement of the defect: SELECT over granny_flat_reports returns 16 rows with confirmed_structure_count, 15 with both counts, 13 agree / 2 disagree / 1 machine-NULL, 0 with any provenance field, and 0 of 87 rows holding detected_structures and a confirmed count together. Both 'disagreements' are confirmed=1 / machine=0, which only the frontend ': 1' fallback produces - a brief-card deselect can only yield confirmed <= machine - so the human-signal count is 0, not the 2 the census recorded. (3) grep on origin/main showed pvlib named in the PDF at shadow-report.tsx:576/583, /how-it-works:74, the audit-trail source string shadow_detector.py:479 and 381 report_audit_trail rows, with zero import sites; and PC_CATALOG/S1_COLLECTION/FLOOD_RATIO each appearing exactly once, at their own definition.
falsifiable_check.mutation_evidence: Delete the `human_checked` term from _compute_confidence's high branch -> test_high_needs_human_reviewed_count and test_compute_confidence_agreement_without_human_is_not_high fail. Default count_source to 'secondary_detections_classified' instead of 'unrecorded' -> test_compute_confidence_default_count_source_is_not_high and test_confirm_records_unrecorded_when_caller_is_silent fail. Drop the onCountChange call from handleStructureType -> three ConfirmationPanel tests fail (the exact regression that shipped originally). Stop persisting structure_types/detect_id/confirmed_count_source -> test_confirm_persists_count_provenance_join_key_and_answers fails. Remove the detected_structures carry-forward -> nothing in Python fails, so the guard is the post_merge SQL check below rather than a unit test; recorded as a known gap. Re-emit 'garage' for kept brief-card structures -> the never-labels-a-type-it-does-not-ask-for test fails. Restore 'pvlib' to the PDF methodology string -> grep 2 in the command goes non-empty. Sol review added three more: drop the deselected-touch filter in the brief card -> 'sends no answers and no review claim when the user touches nothing' fails; remove the detect_id fallback lookup -> test_carry_forward_finds_the_detect_row_by_detect_id fails; delete the model_validator -> test_secondary_detections_classified_without_answers_is_rejected fails. The carry-forward gap noted above as 'no unit test' is now closed by that second test. Sol round 2 added three more: trust the caller's count_source flag instead of resolving it -> the three 'downgraded_when' tests fail; drop `AND prop_id = %s` from the carry-forward -> test_carry_forward_is_scoped_to_the_submitted_parcel fails; restore v1's Jun/Sep-only limitation text -> the disclaimer contradicts SHADOW_SCENARIOS again. Sol round 3 added three more: drop the implied-count check -> test_secondary_detections_classified_is_downgraded_when_the_count_contradicts_the_answers fails; revert to req.samgeo_structure_count as the comparator -> test_machine_count_comes_from_the_detect_row_not_the_client_echo fails; remove the else branch in handleStructureType -> the 'retracts the existing-granny-flat answer' test fails. Sol round 4 added three more: restrict the implied-count check back to the secondary_detections_classified branch -> test_count_contradicting_its_answers_is_flagged_under_any_provenance fails; drop `outputs->>'detect_id' = %s` from the report_id lookup -> test_report_id_lookup_is_bound_to_the_same_detect_run fails; move the duplicate-index check back inside the secondary_detections_classified branch -> test_duplicate_indexes_rejected_under_every_provenance fails. Sol round 5: rename 'secondary_detections_classified' back to 'user_reviewed' and the CountSource comment's own reasoning contradicts the name — the label would again assert a verified total that no surface can produce. Sol round 6: log req.samgeo_structure_count as the SAM response again -> the audit record reports a client-supplied number as the detector's; move the unknown-index check back inside the claim branch -> test_unknown_index_is_flagged_under_any_provenance fails; rename back to detections_classified -> the name again claims coverage of a principal dwelling nobody classified. Sol round 7: drop the coordinate bound from the carry-forward -> test_carry_forward_is_scoped_to_the_submitted_parcel fails; remove the partial-answer branch -> test_partial_answers_are_not_described_as_unchecked fails. Sol round 8: remove the empty-expected refusal -> test_claim_is_refused_when_there_was_nothing_to_classify fails and a lot with no secondary structure earns the classification claim again.
falsifiable_check.self_comparison_note: None of these re-run the code and check it agrees with itself. The pvlib checks read the import graph, which is the authority on whether a library is used. The confidence checks assert against fixed expected values chosen from the semantics, not from the function's current output. The production measurements compare two independently-produced numbers (detector count vs submitted count) and then explain the difference from the frontend source, rather than accepting equality as evidence - which is precisely the trap this change removes.

pre_impl.existing_data: Read-only production census 2026-08-06 before any edit. granny_flat_reports: 87 rows (2026-04-08 to 2026-07-26), 16 with confirmed_structure_count, 15 with both counts, 13 agree / 2 disagree / 1 machine-NULL, 0 with a provenance field, 0 holding detected_structures and a confirmed count together, 8 high / 8 medium. disclaimer_versions: exactly one live shadow row (id=4, shadow-v1) whose source_attributions opens with pvlib. report_audit_trail: 381 rows naming pvlib. property_reports flood: 148 rows, 0 with null or empty data_sources, but 143 still naming Microsoft Planetary Computer S1 RTC (131 inside the 90-day cache window, newest 2026-08-03).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Three inherited claims were wrong and are corrected in the plan docs. (a) The census said 2 rows carry genuine human disagreement; 0 do - both are the ': 1' fallback. (b) It cited the SAR constants at flood_truth.py:100-101/115; on origin/main they sit at :109-110/129, so the stale working tree would have produced wrong citations. (c) It described pvlib as cited on three surfaces; there are more, including 381 audit rows and a QA doc that actively prescribed the false wording as a fix. Additionally, disclaimer_versions.source_attributions is never rendered to a user - audit_trail.py:187 selects only the version column - so migration 064 corrects the evidentiary record, not a page, and the PR says so rather than claiming a user-visible fix.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new module, table, endpoint or data source. granny_flat_reports.inputs/outputs are jsonb, so the four new keys need no schema migration. The detected_structures carry-forward extends the SELECT that already fetched tile_b64 and execution_manifest from the same row by the same id - one more column on an existing query, marked prior-art-checked at the site. Migration 064 follows the lifecycle already documented in migrations/042b and docs/qa/INDEX.md. ConfirmationPanel was exported for test only; its props gained two entries and its local state moved up one level.
pre_impl.external_source_error: pybdshadow is the dependency the corrected wording now names, and it is NOT installed in this environment - so the replacement copy deliberately asserts nothing about its internals. The old docstring claim that pybdshadow 'uses suncalc-py' was dropped rather than restated, because nothing in this repo substantiates it. The new wording claims only what the call site proves: bdshadow_sunlight receives a footprint, a height and a UTC instant and returns the shadow polygon. If the Python API is unreachable the granny-flat confirm route already returns a visible 502; the new fields are optional at every layer so an older client still succeeds, recorded as 'unrecorded'.
pre_impl.frontend_type: structure_types crosses three boundaries. Browser sends {index: number, answer: string}[]. The Next route rejects a non-array, more than 40 entries, a non-integer or out-of-range index, or an answer outside the six literals - HTTP 400, never coercion. Pydantic re-validates against the same Literal set, so a divergence is a 422 rather than a silent drop; both lists include 'kept' and must stay in sync. confirmed_count_source is a three-value union on both sides and an unknown string is rejected rather than defaulted, because defaulting it to 'secondary_detections_classified' would manufacture the exact claim the field exists to make falsifiable. DetectedStructureRow gained an optional index because older brief-card rows may lack it; the payload falls back to array position there. tsc --noEmit passes with 0 errors.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A user marking a detection 'Part of main house' on a 3-structure lot now drops the count to 2, which lifts the MULTIPLE_SECONDARY_STRUCTURES block gating CDC eligibility. That is intended - the block exists because we do not know what the structures are, so it should respond when the user tells us, and leaving it unresponsive is the unwired safeguard this item is about - but it means an answer that previously moved nothing now moves a served verdict. Mitigations: the block only lifts on an explicit per-structure answer; the answer is persisted against the structure index so the decision is auditable after the fact; and a line above the questions states which count will be used and whether it came from the person or the detector. The opposite failure - a report claiming human validation that never happened - is the one being removed, and it was live on 8 reports. Sol round 2 surfaced a failure mode I had created rather than inherited: making the detect_id lookup live turned a previously-dead unscoped query into a cross-property leak. It is now scoped to the submitted prop_id and fails closed.

functions.name: _compute_confidence
functions.input: validated flag, confirmed_count, samgeo_count, rent_available, and now count_source (three-state provenance)
functions.output: (confidence, reason); 'high' only when a person reviewed the count AND it matches the detector AND rent data exists
functions.if_none: count_source absent defaults to 'unrecorded', which cannot reach 'high' - absence is its own state, never folded into 'a human checked'

functions.name: confirm_and_calculate
functions.input: GrannyFlatConfirmRequest, which now also carries the confirmed_count_source provenance value and the per-structure structure_types answers
functions.output: same response contract; the persisted inputs gain confirmed_count_source, structure_types and detect_id, and outputs gain the carried-forward detected_structures
functions.if_none: structure_types None is stored as null (not an empty list, which would read as 'asked and answered nothing'); detect row absent means detected_structures carries forward as null

functions.name: ConfirmationPanel.handleStructureType
functions.input: structure index + one of the four answers
functions.output: lifts the answer to the page AND invokes onCountChange with detected count minus the detections marked part_of_main
functions.if_none: no answers given means onCountChange is never called and the count stays the detector's figure, which the page then transmits as 'machine_default'

functions.name: runConfirm
functions.input: detect result, the already-adjusted count, the per-structure answers
functions.output: confirm POST carrying confirmed_count_source and structure_types; derives provenance only, never re-adjusts the count
functions.if_none: fewer answers than secondary structures yields 'machine_default' - a partial pass is not a review

functions.name: _resolve_count_source
functions.input: the caller's claimed provenance value, the submitted per-structure answers, and the detect run's own detected_structures list
functions.output: (resolved_source, downgrade_note) - 'secondary_detections_classified' survives only when the answers cover every non-main detected structure with no unknown index
functions.if_none: detect row missing or empty -> 'machine_default' with a recorded note; a review that cannot be checked is not credited

values.guard_at: services/granny_flat.py:1259 (`req.confirmed_count_source or "unrecorded"`) and route.ts COUNT_SOURCES membership check returning 400
values.if_missing: 'unrecorded' - confidence capped at medium and the reason says no person reviewed the count

values.guard_at: route.ts array/shape/answer-literal validation returning 400; Pydantic Literal re-validation
values.if_missing: stored as null, distinguishable from an empty list

values.value: detected_structures carried into the confirm row
values.guard_at: initialised to None and only set when the detect row is found by report_id
values.if_missing: null - the confirm row records answers without their referent, the pre-change state for all 87 rows

queries.purpose: carry the detect run's tile, manifest AND per-structure evidence into the confirm row
queries.where_clause: id = %s (unchanged; one additional selected column, outputs->'detected_structures')
queries.if_zero: row absent -> all three carry-forwards stay None, same as before for tile_b64
queries.if_wrong: without this the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE below overwrites the detect row and deletes the structures the stored answers refer to - measured as 0 of 87 rows holding both

queries.where_clause: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE (unchanged); three keys added to the inputs jsonb, one to outputs
queries.if_wrong: a row claiming confirmed_count_source='secondary_detections_classified' with a null structure_types is detectable by the post_merge query and would indicate a caller asserting provenance it did not collect

queries.purpose: supersede the shadow disclaimer that names pvlib
queries.where_clause: pipeline_name='shadow' AND version='shadow-v1' AND superseded_at IS NULL
queries.if_zero: the trailing DO block raises unless exactly one live shadow version remains, so a no-op UPDATE aborts the transaction rather than leaving zero live rows
queries.if_wrong: two live versions would make get_current_disclaimer_version nondeterministic; the same post-condition catches that case

break_it.scenario: the audit trail records the client-echoed samgeo_structure_count as SAM's own response
break_it.what_happens: a request claiming 99 detections makes the evidentiary record say SAM returned 99, with features_returned=99 — the exact class of false attribution this branch exists to remove, sitting inside the defence layer
break_it.how: Sol round-6 finding 1, verified real and fixed: the SAM DataSourceQuery now records machine_count read back from the detect row, and keeps the request's number beside it labelled structure_count_client_echo rather than passing it off as the detector's.

break_it.scenario: 'detections_classified' is claimed when only the SECONDARY structures were answered
break_it.what_happens: the standalone tool never asks about the detector-designated principal dwelling, so the value and the served reason both claimed every detection had been classified when one never was
break_it.how: Sol round-6 finding 2, verified real and fixed: the value is now secondary_detections_classified, matching the coverage rule that has always only required the non-main structures, and both reason strings say 'each secondary structure among them' and name the principal dwelling as detector-identified and outside the check.

break_it.scenario: an answer naming a structure index the detect run never produced is stored under machine_default or unrecorded
break_it.what_happens: a label with no referent is persisted as calibration data, silently — the unknown-index check ran only when the classification claim was made, and a matching implied count meant nothing else fired either
break_it.how: Sol round-6 finding 3, verified real and fixed: the unknown-index and implied-count checks now run whenever a detect row and any answers are both present, before any branch on provenance. Only the coverage check remains claim-specific.

break_it.scenario: a valid (detect_id, prop_id) pair from one property is submitted with another property's address and coordinates
break_it.what_happens: the first property's tile, manifest and detected structures are carried into a report labelled as the second, and can produce confidence from the wrong parcel's evidence
break_it.how: Sol round-7 finding 1, verified real and fixed: both carry-forward lookups now also apply the ~50m coordinate bound the flood cache read already uses (abs(lat-%s) < 0.0005 AND abs(lng-%s) < 0.0005). A mismatch loses the carry-forward and downgrades provenance rather than serving another parcel's evidence.

break_it.scenario: a person classifies some structures, the count moves because of it, and the report says the count has not been checked against the aerial image
break_it.what_happens: the reverse of overclaiming, but still inaccurate — their answers already moved the number the report used
break_it.how: Sol round-7 finding 2, verified real and fixed: a partial-answer branch states how many structures were classified, that the count reflects them, and that the remainder were not — instead of asserting the total was unchecked.

break_it.scenario: a lot where the detector found only a principal dwelling claims secondary_detections_classified
break_it.what_happens: the coverage set is empty, so the check passed vacuously and the claim was granted for a classification that could not have happened — letting a single-dwelling lot reach 'high' on a review of nothing
break_it.how: Sol round-8 finding, verified real and fixed: an empty expected-set is now an explicit refusal with its own note, not a silent pass. Practical consequence, stated: single-dwelling lots can no longer reach 'high', which is correct — there is nothing on such a lot for a person to check.

post_merge.db_reset: No reset. One migration must be applied to production: migrations/064_shadow_disclaimer_v2_pvlib_removal.sql. Expected before: 1 shadow row (id=4, shadow-v1, superseded_at IS NULL). Expected after: 2 shadow rows, exactly one live, version 'shadow-v2'. Until it runs, new shadow reports keep recording version 'shadow-v1', whose stored attributions still name pvlib. Not user-visible either way - source_attributions is never rendered; audit_trail.py:187 selects only the version column.
post_merge.secrets: No new secrets or environment variables.
post_merge.other_repo: No. Trigger.dev reaches the confirm path only through the Next route, whose contract is additive - both new fields are optional at every layer, so an un-updated caller still succeeds and is recorded as 'unrecorded'.
